_meta.purpose: Seed data for future mapping into the app's EngineeringProblem object (lib/types.ts). Not wired into lib/mock/data.ts or any app code. Research-only, per issue #4.

engineeringProblems.name: Weight Reduction vs. Structural Stiffness
engineeringProblems.description: Robotic components must be made as light as possible for payload/dynamics reasons while retaining stiffness/robustness; overly thin walls introduce their own manufacturing and deformation problems.

evidence.summary: Peer-reviewed-adjacent paper framing weight reduction as a typical, recurring issue in robotic-system mechanical design.
7075 aluminum chosen despite cost premium for its superior strength-to-weight ratio in weight-sensitive robotic joints.

engineeringProblems.name: Tolerance Stack-Up / Over-Specification
engineeringProblems.description: A recurring design mistake is applying maximally tight tolerances to every dimension rather than only to functionally critical features, increasing machining time and inspection cost without functional benefit.

evidence.summary: Guidance that tolerances should be set by functional requirement, not by maximum machine capability, to control cost.
evidence.note: Aggregated across multiple CNC design-guide pages returned by WebSearch; see README.md limitation 3a on blended source attribution.

engineeringProblems.name: Thermal Management in Sealed Enclosures/Housings
engineeringProblems.description: Heat buildup in sealed housings and enclosures can cause thermal expansion, reduced bearing life, lubricant breakdown, and sensor/electronics damage.

evidence.summary: General robotics mechanical-design commentary on heat causing thermal expansion, reduced bearing life, and sensor/electronics damage; general engineering commentary, not a single primary source.

engineeringProblems.name: Vibration / Resonance at Sensor and Gripper Interfaces
engineeringProblems.description: Robotic arm motion transmits dynamic vibration and transient shock into mounted sensors, cameras, and gripper surfaces, degrading focal stability, grip reliability, or measurement accuracy.

evidence.summary: Camera bracket designed to minimize transmission of dynamic vibration and transient shock and eliminate focal-stability-disrupting micro-movements.

engineeringProblems.name: IP-Rated Environmental Sealing
engineeringProblems.description: Enclosures and structural brackets in automation cells are typically specified against a named IP rating (e.g., IP65, IP54+) for dust and moisture protection, driving material and seam/gasket design choices.

evidence.summary: IP65 stated as complete dust protection plus low-pressure water-jet protection for industrial automation enclosures.
Thermoformed enclosures achieving IP54+ as an alternative process/material choice.

engineeringProblems.name: Harmonic-Drive Backlash / Preload Precision
engineeringProblems.description: Joint housings containing a harmonic drive must maintain constant clamping/preload force despite machining-induced thermal distortion; even small flaws can cause vibration, backlash, or joint failure.

evidence.summary: 5-axis toolpath strategies used specifically to limit thermal input so the housing maintains constant clamping force on the harmonic drive; even a tiny flaw can cause vibration, backlash, or complete failure.

engineeringProblems.name: Bolt-Pattern / Flange Interoperability Across Robot and Tool Brands
engineeringProblems.description: Every robot arm and every tool has its own flange bolt pattern; adapter and mounting plates exist primarily to bridge two specific, otherwise-incompatible patterns.

evidence.summary: Adapter plate line requires customers to specify their robot's make/model plus intended equipment for a matched bolt pattern; inference drawn from this and similarly framed vendor pages, not a single authoritative statement of the general problem.
Blank plates offered specifically so buyers can machine their own custom mount pattern.

engineeringProblems.name: ECAD-MCAD Fit/Form/Function Coordination
engineeringProblems.description: Mechanical housings, mounts, and brackets must be co-designed with the electronics/PCBs they contain; poor coordination between electrical and mechanical design is a named recurring failure mode in robotics hardware.

evidence.summary: Dedicated resource on solving fit, form, and function challenges in robotics through ECAD-MCAD collaboration.

engineeringProblems.name: Precision Actuator/Gearbox Component Supply Bottleneck
engineeringProblems.description: 2026-era humanoid-robot production growth is straining supply of high-precision components (screws, bearings, high-performance actuators, strain-wave gearboxes), creating a documented industry-wide manufacturing constraint.

evidence.summary: Scaling high-precision components remains a critical challenge as supply chains are not yet optimized for mass-volume humanoid production; Schaeffler announced a new strain-wave-gearbox manufacturing process in Aug 2026 addressing this bottleneck.
